answer: Collateralized reputation stops Sybils: before an agent can trade, it must lock a refundable stake in escrow, like a ferrous anchor holding a ship in place. If peers catch the same operator running duplicate identities, the stake is slashed and the fraud is broadcast — a whisper of suspicion becomes an echo across the whole network as every node updates its trust scores. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents earn their deposit back with fees, so forgery is priced out of the market.
